already-have.corrections: 1) Tracked only as #238 (docs reframe, low priority); the protocol proposal itself is NOT tracked — a new issue would be needed. 2) Load-bearing technical correction to the proposal: as written it does NOT close the stated threat. `sphincs-c10/src/fors.rs:98-131` derives `R = sha256(sk_seed ‖ "R_grind" ‖ opt_rand ‖ M ‖ nonce)[..16]` (secret-keyed) and `hypertree.rs:169-172` writes that R into the signature; the on-chain verifier accepts ANY R (it just recomputes the digest from it). Feeding a host-committed `opt_rand` into a secret-keyed PRF therefore constrains only an honest-but-biased-TRNG device; malicious firmware can return a perfectly honest `(n_dev, opt_rand)` transcript and still set the signature's R to key bits, because no party without `sk_seed` can check R's derivation. The ECDSA anti-exfil guarantee comes from the group homomorphism (`R = R0 + H(R0,e)·G` is host-checkable); hash-based has no analogue. The achievable design is different and heavier: make R publicly derivable — e.g. device commits `H(n_dev)`, host sends `e`, device signs with `R = H(n_dev ‖ e ‖ M ‖ grind_nonce)` (sequential-nonce grind so the host can verify the minimal satisfying nonce) and reveals `n_dev` to the host only. That removes `sk_seed` from `grind_r`, which touches the upstream SPHINCS- "Avenue B" chosen-message FORS-saturation argument (unpredictability must then come from device-fresh `n_dev` committed before `e`), changes a C10 primitive with Lean/EasyCrypt proof assets, and leaves `n_dev` as a device→host (not public) channel — acceptable only if the colluding-companion case is explicitly out of scope. 3) The "target-sum grind freedom" residual is overstated for the honest algorithm: `grind_r` is already a deterministic first-hit scan over `nonce = 0..`, so there is no extra honest freedom; freedom exists only for malicious firmware, which is unconstrained anyway unless R becomes host-verifiable as above. 4) Cost should be re-rated from M upward if the real (R-public) variant is pursued; the as-written variant is cheap but gives roughly zero guarantee against the named adversary. 5) Could not check: companion-side code and the `verify.pqsigner.io` ceremony docs for any existing transcript hook (none found in firmware/proto).

feasible.reason: The proposal does not defend against its own stated threat (malicious firmware / RDP-regressed die). In C10 the 16-byte randomizer R is shipped in the clear and is bound to opt_rand ONLY inside the device: `fors::grind_r` computes R = trunc(sha256(sk_seed ‖ "R_grind" ‖ opt_rand ‖ M ‖ nonce)) (sphincs-c10/src/fors.rs:109-128). Neither the firmware verifier nor the on-chain Yul verifier re-derives R; both just load it from the signature (SPHINCsC10Asm.sol:72 `R := and(calldataload(sig.offset), N_MASK)`) and apply the only observable constraint, `fors_indices[K-1] == 0` (hypertree.rs:179/379, 11 bits). So a malicious image simply ignores opt_rand, writes the seed-bit payload into R, and grinds until the 11-bit forced-zero gate passes: ~117 free bits per signature, exactly the attack #238 describes ("write seed bytes into opt_rand_buf ... grind the nonce"). Committing to opt_rand and returning (n_dev, opt_rand) lets the auditor confirm a value that nothing in the signature depends on; the proposal itself concedes "R = PRF(sk_prf, opt_rand, M) is only checkable by the device" and then still claims a defence. Issue #238 already states the bar: "Proper protocol closure would need verifier-side re-derivation of R or a NIZK that R was honestly derived." The proposal does neither. The second half of the threat, a TRNG-path implant, is not a key-leak threat at all here: R is sk_seed-keyed, so a biased or attacker-known OptRand degrades to deterministic-equivalent signing (still secure in the SPHINCS+ model; crypto.rs:229-235 and hypertree.rs:163-167 say exactly this). The commitment therefore adds nothing against the implant and is bypassed by the malicious image. Secondary: the WOTS+C count is likewise only gated by `sum == TARGET_SUM` (wots.rs:178), so a non-minimal count is a second, smaller channel the proposal only hand-waves ("bound it by fixing the grind nonce schedule") without making it verifier-checkable.
feasible.corrections: A sound version exists but it is a scheme change, not a wire-format add-on, and it carries a cryptographic trade the proposal does not flag: (1) Make R publicly recomputable: R := trunc(sha256(pk_seed ‖ "R_pub" ‖ host_secret ‖ n_dev ‖ M ‖ nonce)) with the MINIMAL nonce that satisfies the forced-zero gate, and require the WOTS+C count per layer to be the MINIMAL count with digit-sum 205. Both minimality rules are host-checkable with a few tens of thousands of SHA-256 (the verifier recomputes from 0), which turns every byte of the 4008-B signature into a canonical function of (sk, M, host_secret, n_dev) — zero-capacity covert channel in signature bytes. Keep the two-round commit (host c=H(host_secret) → device H(n_dev) → host reveals → device signs) so neither side can grind R; the device cannot bias R because it commits n_dev before learning host_secret. The on-chain verifier is unchanged (it never checks R's derivation), so no contract/initCode/address impact. (2) The trade: today's secret-keyed R is the load-bearing "Avenue B" defence (chosen-message FORS-saturation) that holds even under TRNG failure (hypertree.rs:163-167, upstream SECURITY-ANALYSIS §2). With public R, if n_dev is predictable (the very TRNG-implant case the proposal lists), the untrusted companion can predict FORS indices and run the saturation attack. So the design must either accept that the anti-klepto property and TRNG-failure robustness are mutually exclusive for a hash-based signer without a NIZK, or hybridise (e.g. n_dev := TRNG ⊕ PRF(sk_prf, host_secret ‖ M) is NOT verifiable, so no hybrid is available; state it as an owner decision). (3) Residual channels the host cannot see even then: rejection sampling via abort (~1 bit per visible refusal), sign latency (first sign 14-17 s, Type-2 6-7 s, publicly observable to the companion), and the FI double-compute is unaffected (R still drawn/derived once). (4) Feasibility notes: the unified-sign `flags` u32 has NO spare bit (31/30 flags, 29..22 account, 21..0 slot), so versioning must come from an appended, length-checked trailer or a new CMD, and the two-round protocol introduces per-session S-world state (n_dev) that must be bound to the 120 s idle timeout and zeroised — not a hardware change, kind=firmware stands. (5) The Lean/EasyCrypt spec of R (Spec/Fors.lean forced-zero gate, the Avenue-B argument, F-9 TVLA rationale) would have to be re-proved for a public randomizer; cost is L rather than M once that is counted. Priority P2 is defensible only for the corrected design; as written the item should be re-scoped to the docs action #238 already tracks plus a design note that the only firmware-level closure is public-R + minimal-count canonicalisation with the stated trade.

(1) Jade: Blockstream/Jade CHANGELOG.md entry "[0.1.24] - 2021-04-14 / Added: Add support for 'Anti-Exfil' signatures in Jade" and the cited blog post both give 0.1.24 / 2021-04-14 — the proposal's version+year are exact. (2) BitBox02: bitbox02-firmware CHANGELOG.md v9.4.0 (2021-01-20) "Protection against the nonce covert channel attack when singing Bitcoin/Litecoin transactions (antiklepto protocol)", v9.5.0 (2021-03-10) "Anti-klepto support for ETH transaction signing and for BTC and ETH message signing", v9.26.0 made the host nonce commitment optional for EIP-712. (3) Trezor does NOT ship it: 0 commits and 0 source hits for exfil/klepto/nonce-commit in /home/nicola/repos/trezor-firmware; ECDSA nonces are plain RFC6979 (crypto/ecdsa.c:693-710 init_rfc6979/generate_k_rfc6979), which Blockstream's own write-up says cannot defend a malicious wallet. The proposal never claims Trezor ships it, so nothing to refute. (4) Ledger: no source found claiming Ledger ships anti-exfil (ledger.com/blog/dark-skippy 404; app-bitcoin-new search empty) — consistent with the proposal's 'none for Ledger'. (5) novelty='beyond': no PQ wallet or SLH-DSA/SPHINCS+ implementation with a host-committed randomizer was found (searches on SLH-DSA/SPHINCS subliminal/anti-klepto returned only SCA work and generic subversion-resilience theory). Repo evidence verified: secure/src/crypto.rs:205-250 draws OptRand once from rng_strong::fill (STM32⊕OPTIGA⊕SE050, secure/src/rng_strong.rs:185-211) with no host input; gh #238 is OPEN (labels source:work-todo, priority:low, surface:docs); proto/src/lib.rs:1630-1634 pins SIGN_USEROP_HEADER_LEN==330 with no commitment field; the only 'commitment' hits under secure/src/nsc are the unrelated batch tuple commitments (cmd_sign_userop_batch.rs:67,963-1793). The claim is therefore not refuted; the corrections below are precision fixes, not disqualifiers.
vendor-claim.corrections: (a) Precedent is incomplete, not wrong: cite BitBox02 v9.4.0 (2021-01-20, BTC/LTC tx) and v9.5.0 (2021-03-10, ETH tx + BTC/ETH message signing) — BitBox shipped anti-klepto for ETH/ECDSA, i.e. the same ecosystem as PQ1, and v9.26.0 relaxed it for EIP-712 (a usability precedent worth noting for the off-chain path). Jade 0.1.24 / 2021-04-14 is exact. (b) Add the adjacent Trezor precedent correctly: Trezor ships a host commit/reveal protocol ONLY for seed generation ('entropy check': core/src/apps/management/reset_device/__init__.py:100-107 computes entropy_commitment = HMAC-SHA256(int_entropy, ''), proto common/protob/messages-management.proto:535-538, python/src/trezorlib/device.py:337-413) — same two-round pattern the proposal wants, but not for signatures. Do not describe Trezor as having any signing-nonce commitment. (c) The rationale's parenthetical 'upstream SPHINCS- analysis already flags it' is wrong: ~/repos/SPHINCS-/docs/SECURITY-ANALYSIS.md has no klepto/subliminal/exfil/covert mention; it only says R 'may optionally be hedged by folding fresh opt_rand into the preimage' (line ~92). The covert-channel flag is PQ1's own gh #238. (d) The protocol text 'R = PRF(sk_prf, opt_rand, M)' is not C10: R = sha256(sk_seed‖"R_grind"‖opt_rand‖M‖nonce_be32)[0..16], ground over nonce until the last FORS index is zero (sphincs-c10/src/fors.rs:70,98-131; hypertree.rs:163-173). Consequence: even with host-committed opt_rand a malicious signer keeps a secret-keyed grind — it may pick a LATER satisfying nonce (one per ~2^11 trials), leaking ≈log2(candidates tried) bits/sig; no auditor can detect this because sk_seed is in the preimage. This is exactly the 'churn the final R' residual moonsettler states for the non-interactive scheme (delvingbitcoin.org/t/1081, 2024-08-20) and the libwally 'selective abort' caveat (restart only with the same rho; >~20 aborts ever = switch vendor). State the achievable guarantee as 'device cannot choose opt_rand; bounded residual via R-nonce choice and abort/retry', not 'no covert channel'. (e) The proposal's 'target-sum grind consumes additional freedom' is understated AND partly closable without a wire change: the WOTS+C count (4 B per layer, d=2, embedded in the signature at hypertree.rs:310-312; contracts/smart-wallet/src/verifiers/SPHINCsC10Asm.sol:154-161 reads it) is derived from PUBLIC inputs only — wots_digest(pk_seed, adrs, msg_hash, count) (sphincs-c10/src/hash.rs:350-360, hash.rs:55 'wots_digest — public'), and the honest signer takes the FIRST count with digit-sum 205 (wots.rs:63-80), but pk_from_sig (wots.rs:157-180) checks only sum==TARGET_SUM, not minimality. So today the count is a signer-chosen public field (a second covert channel, ~log2(k) bits per layer per sig for k candidates tried) that an off-chain auditor/companion can close by re-grinding and asserting minimality — cheap, protocol-free, and should be listed as a companion-side check in the same improvement. On-chain minimality enforcement is too gas-expensive; keep it auditor-side. (f) 'novelty: beyond' is accurate as 'first application to a hash-based/PQ signer', but the mechanism is not novel: anti-exfil (Jade/BitBox 2021), the 2020 bitcoin-dev 'anti-covert-channel signing' schemes, the non-interactive variant (moonsettler 2024), and subversion-resilient signatures (Ateniese–Magri–Venturi CCS 2015) are prior art; phrase novelty accordingly. (g) gh #238 is labelled priority:low/surface:docs and itself says protocol closure is 'an open research direction'; promoting it to a P2 firmware item should reference the issue and either relabel it or open a sibling implementation issue. (h) Minor: repo_evidence line range should be crypto.rs:205-250 (comment block 205-237, the fill call and partial-scrub at ~240-250).
